needs_human.note: The tag filter is now scoped to the listed drive's Tag rows, so stale-linked files drop out of the listing. This rests on no SPEC or UNSPEC statement that covers stale links.; Coexisting variants in one drive: each sidebar row shows its own count (`Übung` 1, `übung` 1) while choosing either lists both files (2 items). The UNSPEC at test_tag_name_matching.py:56 states the listing rule, and no rule states the count disagreement; decisions.md step 7 observed it.; A case-variant name on a note renames the one shared row for all files in the drive, while batch tagging a non-Markdown file keeps the existing spelling. A batch mixing .md and other files therefore treats the same request differently. This matches the existing ASCII behaviour and is newly reachable for non-ASCII names.; Matching uses Python str.lower(), not casefold: `STRASSE` and `straße` stay different tags, and Greek final sigma makes `ΣΑΣ` lower to `σας`, which differs from `σασ`. Tests pin only the lower() rule.

A file with a stale link to another drive's Tag row shows a chip for that tag, but the chip's ?tag= listing on the file's own drive leaves the file out. Neither a test nor known-issues.md:74-78 records this.; A cross-drive move removes rows on the destination that were already unreferenced when the moved file holds a stale link to that drive. Only the one test at test_tag_name_matching.py:167-180 records this.
